headline_marked: [[Govt to bear Tk 70/litre loss on diesel]] despite recent price hike: Rizvi
headline: Govt to bear Tk 70/litre loss on diesel despite recent price hike: Rizvi
summary: The government has no alternative but to adjust fuel prices due to the international market, but will still cover a significant loss through subsidies. This hike is expected to put pressure on citizens.
details: BNP Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi stated that the government will still incur a loss of approximately Tk 70 per litre of diesel, even after raising the fuel price by Tk 20. He explained that this remaining loss must be covered through subsidies.

Rizvi emphasized that the government has no alternative but to adjust fuel prices due to the prevailing international market situation. He made these remarks during a press conference held at the BNP central office in Dhaka's Nayapaltan.

According to Rizvi's calculations, Bangladesh purchases diesel at around Tk 205 per litre. Before the recent Tk 20 increase, the government was bearing a loss of about Tk 90 per litre, which will now reduce to approximately Tk 70 per litre.

Bangladesh consumes about seven million tonnes of fuel annually, with diesel accounting for roughly 4.5 million tonnes. Rizvi acknowledged that higher fuel prices would burden the public but stressed the need to view the issue within global market realities, attributing the hike to a worsening situation in the Middle East.

He urged opposition parties, currently protesting fuel, gas, and electricity shortages, to not only criticize but also propose solutions for addressing these problems, including how to supply fuel at a lower cost.

Rizvi also alleged that recent incidents of violence and arson were orchestrated to divert public attention from the elected government's development initiatives. He questioned the involvement of forces other than the ousted Awami League and accused supporters of the previous government still within the administration of attempting sabotage.

headline_marked: [[MP Gazi Nazrul Islam remanded]] for 4 days over second wife Mariam's alleged abetment of suicide
headline: MP Gazi Nazrul Islam remanded for 4 days over second wife Mariam's alleged abetment of suicide
summary: A Dhaka court ordered the remand of Satkhira-4 MP Gazi Nazrul Islam and his first wife following a case filed by Mariam Khatun's father, who alleges physical and mental abuse led to her death.
details: A Dhaka court has placed Satkhira-4 MP Gazi Nazrul Islam on a four-day remand and his first wife Maksuda Begum on a one-day remand. This action follows a case filed over the alleged abetment of the death by suicide of the lawmaker’s second wife, Mariam Khatun. Police had requested a seven-day remand.

According to case documents, Gazi Nazrul and Maksuda allegedly subjected Mariam to physical and mental abuse. Mariam reportedly informed her family about these issues multiple times over the phone. Gazi Nazrul denies the allegations, stating he was not home during the incident.

Mariam, 19, was found hanging inside a flat at NAM Bhaban, opposite the Jatiya Sangsad, on Sunday afternoon. Her father, SM Masum Billah, lodged the case with Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station, accusing Gazi Nazrul, Maksuda, and Mariam’s maternal uncle Obaidur Rahman.

Mariam’s father, SM Masum Billah, expressed his desire for a proper investigation and justice for his daughter. He stated at the morgue that those responsible should be punished. He also mentioned that his daughter had not responded much when he tried to speak to her directly.

Masum Billah also implicated Obaidur, Mariam's maternal uncle and the lawmaker's driver. He quoted Mariam as saying, "How can I show my face in public? He is my uncle. I didn’t know he would do me such harm. Please forgive me. I used to trust him more than my own father. I am suffering now because I believed him."

Local BNP and Jamaat leaders, along with members of the Shyamnagar Upazila Conscious Citizens’ Forum, have demanded exemplary punishment for Gazi Nazrul. Demonstrations were held, including throwing shoes at and setting fire to an effigy of the MP, calling for a neutral investigation.

This development follows earlier controversy when video clips of Gazi Nazrul and Mariam circulated online, leading to his expulsion from Jamaat for alleged moral misconduct. Obaidur had also filed an attempted murder case against Gazi Nazrul and others.
